from_notes: - **First ruler after the Delhi Sultanate to issue a gold coin: Humayun** (Ghatna Chakra; UKPSC 2012 key gave Akbar); Sher Shah also struck gold.
from_notes_src: notes/row-128.md sub 0 - app notes 1:128 sub 1 (Ghatna Chakra explanation); NextGen Rocket Sheets Indian History Part 1 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.txt) p.101
x: Humayun is credited as the first ruler after the Delhi Sultanate to issue a gold coin; Sher Shah struck gold coins after him, and Akbar later still. (Official UKPSC key: Akbar.)
source: app notes 1:128 sub 1 (Ghatna Chakra explanation); NextGen Rocket Sheets Indian History Part 1 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.txt) p.101
evidence: Rocket p.101: Sher Shah currency of pure gold, silver and copper (no 'first gold coin' claim)
dispute: The official UKPSC key and most books give Akbar, whose mohur established regular gold coinage. Some sources credit Humayun with the first Mughal gold coin after the Sultanate.
